preamble: The alveolar trill [r] can be replaced by a voiceless uvular fricative [χ], shifting the place of articulation back to the uvula and losing both trilling and voicing. The change is typical of the 'strong r' of Portuguese, where the classical trill [r] has given way to uvular [ʁ]/[χ] in Europe and to voiceless back fricatives in Brazil.
sources: Mateus, M. H., & d'Andrade, E. (2000). The Phonology of Portuguese. Oxford University Press. https://academic.oup.com/book/48273
